note.label: Psalm 53: The Fool Says There Is No God

precepts.why:
“The fool hath said in his heart, There is no God.” Paul shows the fool has no excuse: “Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God hath shewed it unto them.” What may be known of God is manifest in them; he showed it. The invisible things are clearly seen in the creation.

The fool knows better. Same-sex relationship people know the Most High said not to do that, which is why they get upset at the scriptures. They are corrupt and have done abominable iniquity, and it is with knowledge.

note.label: Psalm 53: The Fool Says There Is No God

precepts.why: “For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse”. His eternal power and Godhead are understood by the things that are made. The fool who says in his heart there is no God is without excuse; the creation itself shows him. That is why the corrupt who have done abominable iniquity get upset at the scriptures: they know.

precepts.text: When they knew God, they glorified him not as God, but became vain in their imaginations; spelling his name with a little "g," calling him "the man upstairs," or "mother nature," which does not exist.

note.label: Psalm 53: The Fool Says There Is No God

precepts.why:
“Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened.” They knew God and glorified him not as God. That is spelling his name with a little g, calling him the man upstairs, or mother nature, which does not exist. Vain imaginations, and a foolish heart darkened.

That is the fool of Psalm 53 who says in his heart there is no God: not one who never knew, but one who knew and would not glorify him.

note.label: Psalm 53: The Fool Says There Is No God

precepts.why: “Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools”. The ones who say there is no God profess to be wise, but the Most High calls them fools, the same word David uses: “The fool hath said in his heart, There is no God.” They knew God from the creation, glorified him not, became vain in their imaginations, and in their wisdom became fools. Corrupt are they, and there is none that doeth good.

note.label: Psalm 53: The Fool Says There Is No God

precepts.why:
Before Sodom, he looked down in the days of Noah: “And God saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and that every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually.” When he looked, he saw wickedness, and every imagination of the thoughts of man's heart only evil continually.

This is how we differ from the world: keeping the Commandments. God looks down to see if there are any that understand and seek him, and the ones keeping his Commandments are the ones he finds.
